docs.title: CareFlow API
docs.text:
Welcome to the CareFlow API documentation.

CareFlow is a fictional platform that connects home care companies with licensed healthcare professionals — including physicians, nurses, occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and other specialists in the home care ecosystem. The API enables organizations to securely create, manage, and retrieve professional records through a structured REST interface.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
The CareFlow API is designed for secure, scalable integrations. Before making requests, clients should:

  • Obtain a valid access token
  • Understand authentication requirements
  • Implement proper error handling
  • Respect API usage limits

All communication occurs over HTTPS using JSON-formatted requests and responses.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
https://api.careflow.dev/v1

API versioning ensures long-term compatibility as the platform evolves.

docs.title: Available Resources
docs.text:
• Professionals — manage healthcare professional records
  • Authentication — secure access to protected endpoints
  • Error Handling — consistent error reporting and recovery guidance

Each section provides detailed request formats, response examples, and integration best practices.

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
The CareFlow API follows modern REST principles:

  • Predictable resource-oriented URLs
  • Standard HTTP status codes
  • Stateless request handling
  • Consistent JSON data structures

This approach ensures reliable integration with healthcare workflows and third-party systems.

For detailed implementation guidance, refer to the individual resource sections.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The CareFlow API uses token-based authentication to secure access to protected resources. Every request to a protected endpoint must include a valid access token in the HTTP Authorization header.

Requests without authentication — or with an invalid token — will be rejected.

docs.title: Authentication Method
docs.text: CareFlow uses Bearer token authentication over HTTPS.

docs.title: Header format
docs.text: Authorization: Bearer

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
GET /professionals HTTP/1.1
Host: api.careflow.dev
Authorization: Bearer cf_live_9f3a7b21c4e8d12a
Content-Type: application/json

docs.title: Token Lifecycle
docs.text:
Access tokens are issued by the CareFlow platform and are tied to a specific organization.

Tokens should be:

  • Stored securely
  • Never exposed in client-side code
  • Rotated periodically

If a token is compromised, it should be revoked immediately.

docs.title: Authentication Errors
docs.text: The API returns standard HTTP status codes for authentication failures.

docs.title: Unauthorized Request
docs.text:
Status: 401 Unauthorized

{
  "error": "authentication_required",
  "message": "A valid access token must be provided."
}

docs.title: Invalid Token
docs.text:
Status: 403 Forbidden

{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "message": "The provided token is invalid or expired."
}

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always use HTTPS when making API requests
  • Store tokens in secure server-side environments
  • Avoid logging tokens in plaintext
  • Rotate credentials regularly

Failure to follow security best practices may expose sensitive data.

docs.title: cURL Examples
docs.text:
This section demonstrates how to interact with the CareFlow API using curl. These examples simulate real-world usage scenarios, including authentication, creating records, and retrieving data.

All examples assume:

  • Base URL: https://api.careflow.dev/v1
  • A valid Bearer token is available

Replace YOUR_API_TOKEN with your actual token before running the commands.

docs.title: Authentication Header Template
docs.text:
All protected endpoints require an Authorization header:

-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"

docs.title: Create a Healthcare Professional
docs.text:
Registers a new healthcare professional.

curl -X POST https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "fullName": "Dr. Sarah Mitchell",
    "profession": "Physician",
    "licenseNumber": "MD-458721",
    "specialty": "Geriatric Care",
    "contact": {
      "email": "sarah.mitchell@example.com",
      "phone": "+1-555-0142"
    },
    "location": {
      "city": "Chicago",
      "state": "IL"
    },
    "availabilityStatus": "active"
  }'

Expected response:

{
  "id": "prof_8f29a1",
  "status": "created"
}

docs.title: List Healthcare Professionals
docs.text:
Retrieves all registered professionals.

curl -X GET https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"

Example response:

[
  {
    "id": "prof_8f29a1",
    "fullName": "Dr. Sarah Mitchell",
    "profession": "Physician",
    "specialty": "Geriatric Care",
    "location": {
      "city": "Chicago",
      "state": "IL"
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Filter Professionals by Specialty
docs.text:
Query professionals by specialty.

curl -X GET "https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals?specialty=Geriatric%20Care" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"

docs.title: Retrieve a Single Professional
docs.text:
Fetch detailed information about one professional.

curl -X GET https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals/prof_8f29a1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"

docs.title: Update Professional Information
docs.text:
Modify an existing record.

curl -X PATCH https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals/prof_8f29a1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "availabilityStatus": "inactive"
  }'

docs.title: Delete a Professional Record
docs.text:
Remove a professional from the system.

curl -X DELETE https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals/prof_8f29a1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"

Expected response:

204 No Content

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If authentication fails:

401 Unauthorized

Verify:

  • Authorization header format
  • Token validity
  • Token expiration

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always send JSON payloads with Content-Type: application/json.
  • Protect API tokens — never commit them to version control.
  • Test endpoints incrementally when debugging requests.

These examples provide a practical starting point for integrating with the CareFlow API using command-line tools.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The CareFlow API uses conventional HTTP status codes to indicate the success or failure of a request. When an error occurs, the API returns a structured JSON response describing what went wrong.

Clients should always inspect both the HTTP status code and the response body to properly handle failures.

docs.title: Error Response Format
docs.text:
All errors follow a consistent structure:

{
  "error": "error_code",
  "message": "Human-readable description of the error."
}
  • error — machine-readable identifier
  • message — explanation intended for developers

docs.title: 400 — Bad Request
docs.text:
The request is malformed or contains invalid parameters.

{
  "error": "invalid_request",
  "message": "One or more request parameters are invalid."
}

docs.title: 401 — Unauthorized
docs.text:
Authentication credentials are missing.

{
  "error": "authentication_required",
  "message": "A valid access token must be provided."
}

docs.title: 403 — Forbidden
docs.text:
Authentication succeeded, but the token lacks permission.

{
  "error": "insufficient_permissions",
  "message": "You do not have access to this resource."
}

docs.title: 404 — Not Found
docs.text:
The requested resource does not exist.

{
  "error": "resource_not_found",
  "message": "The requested professional could not be found."
}

docs.title: 409 — Conflict
docs.text:
The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.

{
  "error": "resource_conflict",
  "message": "A professional with this identifier already exists."
}

docs.title: 429 — Too Many Requests
docs.text:
Rate limits have been exceeded.

{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "Too many requests. Please try again later."
}

docs.title: 500 — Internal Server Error
docs.text:
An unexpected error occurred on the server.

{
  "error": "internal_error",
  "message": "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again."
}

docs.title: Best Practices for Error Handling
docs.text:
• Always check the HTTP status code
  • Parse the error object for actionable information
  • Implement retries for transient failures
  • Respect rate limit responses

Proper error handling improves system reliability and user experience.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The CareFlow API provides programmatic access to professional management features within the CareFlow platform. It enables organizations to create, retrieve, and manage healthcare professional records in a secure and consistent manner.

This API is designed around REST principles, using predictable resource-oriented URLs and standard HTTP semantics.

docs.title: API Design Principles
docs.text: The CareFlow API follows modern API design conventions to ensure reliability, clarity, and scalability.

docs.title: RESTful Architecture
docs.text:
Resources are accessed via standard HTTP methods:

  • GET — retrieve data
  • POST — create resources
  • PUT/PATCH — update resources
  • DELETE — remove resources

docs.title: JSON Communication
docs.text:
All request and response bodies use JSON encoding.

Content-Type: application/json

Clients should ensure proper serialization and validation before sending requests.

docs.title: Stateless Requests
docs.text: Each API request is independent and must contain all required authentication and parameters. The server does not store client session state.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
All API requests should be made to:

https://api.careflow.dev/v1

Versioning ensures backward compatibility as the platform evolves.

docs.title: Resource Model
docs.text:
The API is organized around logical resources. Each resource represents a domain entity within the CareFlow platform.

Example resources include:

  • Professionals
  • Organizations
  • Credentials

Each resource supports a defined set of operations consistent with REST conventions.

docs.title: Response Behavior
docs.text:
Successful responses return structured JSON data along with appropriate HTTP status codes.

Errors follow a consistent format documented in the Error Handling section.

docs.title: Reliability Expectations
docs.text:
Clients should implement:

  • Proper error handling
  • Retry strategies for transient failures
  • Respect for rate limits
  • Secure authentication practices

These behaviors ensure stable integration with the CareFlow platform.

docs.title: Professionals
docs.text:
The Professionals resource represents licensed healthcare providers registered within the CareFlow platform. Organizations use this resource to manage professional records, credentials, and availability.

All professional data must comply with internal validation and healthcare data integrity rules.

docs.title: Create Professional
docs.text: Creates a new healthcare professional record.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: POST /professionals

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
{
  "fullName": "Dr. Maria Santos",
  "licenseNumber": "NY-458921",
  "profession": "Physician",
  "specialty": "Geriatrics",
  "contact": {
    "email": "maria.santos@example.com",
    "phone": "+1-212-555-0198"
  },
  "location": {
    "city": "New York",
    "state": "NY"
  },
  "availabilityStatus": "active"
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text: Field Type Description fullName string Legal name of the professional licenseNumber string Government-issued professional license profession string Healthcare role (e.g., Physician, Nurse, Therapist) specialty string Area of clinical specialization contact.email string Primary professional email contact.phone string Professional phone number location.city string Service city location.state string Service state availabilityStatus string active, inactive, or suspended

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
• License number must be unique
  • Email must follow RFC format
  • Required fields cannot be empty
  • Availability status must be a valid enum value

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text:
201 — Created

{
  "id": "prof_839201",
  "status": "created"
}

docs.title: Possible Errors
docs.text:
• 400 — Invalid input data
  • 409 — Duplicate license number
  • 401 — Unauthorized

docs.title: Retrieve Professional
docs.text: Fetches a single professional record.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: GET /professionals/{id}

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text:
200 — OK

{
  "id": "prof_839201",
  "fullName": "Dr. Maria Santos",
  "licenseNumber": "NY-458921",
  "profession": "Physician",
  "specialty": "Geriatrics",
  "contact": {
    "email": "maria.santos@example.com",
    "phone": "+1-212-555-0198"
  },
  "location": {
    "city": "New York",
    "state": "NY"
  },
  "availabilityStatus": "active"
}

docs.title: List Professionals
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of professionals.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: GET /professionals

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description profession string Filter by healthcare role specialty string Filter by specialty city string Filter by service location availabilityStatus string Availability filter page integer Pagination index limit integer Results per page

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text: GET /professionals?profession=Physician&city=New York&page=1&limit=20

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text:
200 — OK

{
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 20,
  "total": 142,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "prof_839201",
      "fullName": "Dr. Maria Santos",
      "profession": "Physician",
      "specialty": "Geriatrics",
      "location": {
        "city": "New York",
        "state": "NY"
      },
      "availabilityStatus": "active"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Update Professional
docs.text: Updates an existing professional record.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: PATCH /professionals/{id}

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
{
  "availabilityStatus": "inactive"
}

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text:
200 — OK

{
  "id": "prof_839201",
  "status": "updated"
}

docs.title: Delete Professional
docs.text: Removes a professional record.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: DELETE /professionals/{id}

docs.title: Success Response
docs.text:
204 — No Content

No response body returned.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Validate licensing information before submission
  • Use pagination when listing large datasets
  • Handle duplicate records gracefully
  • Cache read operations when appropriate

Proper management of professional data ensures reliable healthcare workflows within the CareFlow ecosystem.

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: This quickstart walks you through integrating with the CareFlow API in just a few minutes. By the end, you will authenticate, create a healthcare professional record, and retrieve it using command-line tools.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have:

  • A valid CareFlow API token
  • curl installed on your system
  • Internet access

All examples assume the base API endpoint:

https://api.careflow.dev/v1

docs.title: Step 1 — Set Your API Token
docs.text: For convenience, store your API token in an environment variable.

docs.title: macOS / Linux
docs.text: export CAREFLOW_TOKEN=YOUR_API_TOKEN

docs.title: Windows (PowerShell)
docs.text:
setx CAREFLOW_TOKEN "YOUR_API_TOKEN"

Restart your terminal after setting the variable.

docs.title: Step 2 — Verify Authentication
docs.text:
Test that your token is valid by requesting the professionals list.

curl -X GET https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAREFLOW_TOKEN"

If authentication succeeds, you will receive either an empty array or existing records.

Example response:

[]

If authentication fails:

401 Unauthorized

Verify your token and header format.

docs.title: Step 3 — Create a Healthcare Professional
docs.text:
Register a new professional in the system.

curl -X POST https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAREFLOW_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "fullName": "Dr. Emily Carter",
    "profession": "Physician",
    "licenseNumber": "MD-902134",
    "specialty": "Home Geriatric Care",
    "contact": {
      "email": "emily.carter@example.com",
      "phone": "+1-555-0198"
    },
    "location": {
      "city": "Boston",
      "state": "MA"
    },
    "availabilityStatus": "active"
  }'

Expected response:

{
  "id": "prof_a17c29",
  "status": "created"
}

Save the returned id — you will use it next.

docs.title: Step 4 — Retrieve the Created Record
docs.text:
Replace the ID with the one returned above.

curl -X GET https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals/prof_a17c29 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAREFLOW_TOKEN"

Example response:

{
  "id": "prof_a17c29",
  "fullName": "Dr. Emily Carter",
  "profession": "Physician",
  "specialty": "Home Geriatric Care",
  "availabilityStatus": "active"
}

docs.title: Step 5 — Update Availability
docs.text:
Modify an existing field.

curl -X PATCH https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals/prof_a17c29 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAREFLOW_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "availabilityStatus": "inactive"
  }'

docs.title: Step 6 — Clean Up (Optional)
docs.text:
Remove the record when testing is complete.

curl -X DELETE https://api.careflow.dev/v1/professionals/prof_a17c29 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAREFLOW_TOKEN"

Expected response:

204 No Content

docs.text:

  • Implement automated workflows
  • Integrate with backend systems
  • Build internal dashboards
  • Extend professional management features

Refer to the full documentation for advanced usage, authentication details, and error handling.

You are ready to build with CareFlow.
